entries.name: Start of Ramadan
entries.capsule: First day of the month of dawn-to-sunset fasting observed by Muslim Minnesotans, including many Arabic speakers.
entries.dateRule: First day of the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar; set by moon sighting or by the calculation a mosque follows, so the day can differ by one day between mosques.

dates.source: Sahan Journal: Ramadan begins the evening of Tuesday, Feb. 17, 2026, in North America (first fast Feb. 18); Morocco World News gives Feb. 18 as the first day of fasting. Moon-sighted, so some mosques may differ.
Estimated with the Umm al-Qura tabular calendar (hijridate 2.6); Minnesota mosques decide by local or global moon sighting or by calculation, so the observed day can differ by one day.

entries.whatItMarks: The start of the month in which Muslims believe the Quran was revealed, observed by fasting, prayer, Quran reading and charity.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: In 2026 Sahan Journal reported Ramadan began the evening of Feb. 17 and listed public iftars and fundraisers at mosques, community centers and businesses across the Twin Cities. The Lake Street Council said the month 'feels different' in 2026 because of federal immigration enforcement. Observance is shared across Somali, Arab, South Asian and other Muslim Minnesotans.
